messages:
zara_support: FYI — customer ACME-prod is seeing a sudden spike in latency and a flurry of 401s starting ~14:11 UTC. They say traffic for eu-west-1 was routed to us-east-2 during a capacity event. example request id: req_0a3b9f. Attached snippet from their failing response: `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm=\"redwood\", scope=\"eu-west-1\"`

mira: Can you paste a failing response header body and the SDK/user-agent? also which route/model were they hitting?

zara_support: They hit /v1/generate (gpt-echo-prod) from eu-west-1 zone. Customer shows 307 -> us-east-2 then `401 Token scope mismatch`. Here's the curl they used:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -H 'X-Client-Region: eu-west-1' \
  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

sam_t: This looks like the automatic spillover path. If eu-west pool queue depth > spill_threshold we reroute to next region. Token scopes are region-anchored for hosted tokens which explains the 401 on cross-region.

jordan_oncall: Pinging infra: can someone check the autoscaler / routing logs for eu-west-1 around 14:10-14:15? we need to know if it was capacity exhaustion or a mis-evaluated health check.

autoscale-bot: [14:12:27Z] eu-west-1/gpt-pool: active_gpus=48/49, queue_depth=632, spillover_triggered=true -> routed to us-east-2. policy=region_priority, fallback=max_throughput.

alex_k: Confirmed: eu-west had a short-lived enqueue burst, hit the per-pool max_inflight config, autoscaler did not spin up fast enough and the router activated spillover. Two issues: 1) tokens scoped to region cause auth failures when routed cross-region; 2) customer is on strict pinning disabled so they got spilled.

mira: For repro I can simulate by throttling eu-west pool and sending 600 concurrent requests with header `X-Client-Region: eu-west-1`. If that reproduces, we can test mitigations: honor region pin, reissue token with global scope, or add a transparent token-exchange step for hosted users.

zara_support: ACME is sensitive to latency — when routed to us-east-2 p95 went from 120ms -> 920ms and they saw billing jump ~+32% in cost due to longer execution. They want a short-term rollback to stop spillover for their account. Ticket #INC-6238 created.

sam_t: Quick mitigation: set customer region_pin=true (will force reject instead of spill to other regions) and surface 429/503 instead of 401. I can apply a per-tenant policy; needs ops approval for immediate change.

jordan_oncall: I'll apply a temporary pin for ACME on the routing plane and coordinate with billing to waive the excess. Also opening internal task to add a token-exchange shim so we don't 401 on cross-region fallback.

alex_k: Followups: (1) investigate autoscaler pod startup latency and consider lowering spill_threshold by 10% for eu-west pool; (2) review token scope policy for hosted tokens and design exchange flow; (3) confirm SLA/billing adjustment for ACME.

mira: Repro steps I recorded: 1) create 600 concurrent POSTs to /v1/generate with region header; 2) watch router logs for `spillover_triggered`; 3) observe 401 with WWW-Authenticate scope eu-west-1 when routed away. Attaching minimal shell repro:```bash
for i in {1..600}; do 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'X-Client-Region: eu-west-1' \
    -d '{"prompt":"test"}' &
done; wait
```

zara_support: ACME confirmed temporary pin fixed their immediate issue; latency returned to normal after we pinned. They asked for a postmortem/why autoscaler lagged.

jordan_oncall: Assigning follow-ups: ENG-1824 (autoscaler startup tuning), ENG-1825 (regional token-exchange shim), BILL-409 (customer credit for spillover). I'll sync with infra and product.

sam_t: I'll draft a short KB for support: how to pin region for customers and the tradeoffs (reject vs spill).

zara_support: Closing loop with customer; will CC you all on the postmortem once we have root cause. Thanks. :white_check_mark:
